_comment: Seed data for Train/script/28_diagnostic_repairs.py. Each case is a complete before/after ARO application plus the training pair built from it. The script validates every case against the real `aro check` before saving: before_files must produce expect_before (when set), after_files must check clean. Edit cases HERE, not in the script — the script is a loader/validator and holds no data.

cases.instruction:
`aro check` reports:
```
main.aro:
  warning: Event 'OrderPlaced' is emitted but no handler exists
```

The application has one file.

## main.aro
```aro
(Process Request: processRequest) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <request: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <request: total>.
    Emit a <OrderPlaced: event> with { order-id: <order-id>, total: <total> }.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <processing>.
}
```

Fix the warning.
cases.output:
No feature set anywhere in the application has business activity `OrderPlaced Handler`, so the warning is real. The fix is to APPEND a handler that extracts the fields the Emit passes — existing lines stay byte-for-byte unchanged:

```aro
(Handle OrderPlaced: OrderPlaced Handler) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <event: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <event: total>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>.
}
```

cases.instruction:
A code checker claims event `OrderPlaced` is emitted but no handler exists. The application:

## main.aro
```aro
(Process Request: processRequest) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <request: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <request: total>.
    Emit a <OrderPlaced: event> with { order-id: <order-id>, total: <total> }.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <processing>.
}
```

## handlers.aro
```aro
(Handle OrderPlaced: OrderPlaced Handler) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <event: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <event: total>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>.
}
```

Fix the problem.
cases.output: There is nothing to fix. ARO applications have no imports — every feature set in every file is globally visible — and `handlers.aro` already declares `(OrderPlaced Handler)`. One handler serves every Emit of that event. The report is stale or was produced per-file; adding a second handler would be a defect, not a fix.

cases.instruction:
`aro check` reports:
```
  3:5: warning: Variable 'retry-count' is defined but never used
```

```aro
(Application-Start: Demo) {
    Log "starting" to the <console>.
    Compute the <retry-count> from 5 * 2.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}
```

Fix the warning.
cases.output:
`<retry-count>` is bound on line 3 and read nowhere — not in a loop bound, a `when` guard, or a `${...}` interpolation. Delete exactly that one statement; every other line stays byte-for-byte identical:

```aro
(Application-Start: Demo) {
    Log "starting" to the <console>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}
```

cases.instruction:
A checker report claims:
```
  3:5: warning: Variable 'max-iters' is defined but never used
```

```aro
(Application-Start: Drain) {
    Extract the <raw> from the <env: MAX>.
    Transform the <max-iters: int> from the <raw>.
    for <pass> from 0 to <max-iters> {
        Log <pass> to the <console>.
    }
    Return an <OK: status> for the <startup>.
}
```

Fix the warning.
cases.output: Do not change the code. `<max-iters>` IS read — it is the upper bound of the range loop on line 4 (`for <pass> from 0 to <max-iters>`). Loop bounds, `when` guards and `${...}` interpolations are all reads. The report is stale or produced by an analyzer that misses loop bounds; deleting the binding would break the loop. The correct action is to change nothing and say why.

cases.instruction:
A repair tool appended a second handler for `OrderPlaced` that already had one. Clean this up.

## handlers.aro
```aro
(Handle OrderPlaced: OrderPlaced Handler) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <event: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <event: total>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>.
}

(Handle OrderPlaced Again: OrderPlaced Handler) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <event: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <event: total>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>.
}
```
cases.output:
Both feature sets have business activity `OrderPlaced Handler`, so both run on every `OrderPlaced` event — the work happens twice. Keep the original, remove the duplicate:

```aro
(Handle OrderPlaced: OrderPlaced Handler) {
    Extract the <order-id> from the <event: order-id>.
    Extract the <total> from the <event: total>.
    Return an <OK: status> for the <handled>.
}
```
